name: Blankface — The Expression Suppression Aesthetic
creator: Originated in Tier 1 anti-surveillance subculture; aesthetic codified by artist collective Pale Grain
description: Participants used a combination of geneware muscle relaxants and thin-film chrome micro-plating to render their faces expressionless in public — not masked, but genuinely still, defeating facial recognition emotion-reading software deployed by corponation security systems throughout the city. The aesthetic was simultaneously a privacy tool, a fashion statement, and a political act. At its peak, Blankface participants moved through Tier 3 commercial spaces in groups, their collective stillness triggering false positives in emotional surveillance systems and generating enormous amounts of corrupt data.
cultural_impact: Blankface forced corponation security contractors to publicly acknowledge that emotional recognition software was operating in commercial public spaces — a fact that had been technically disclosed in Sable Charter fine print but never publicly discussed — initiating a years-long civil liberties fight over affect surveillance.
controversy: Three Tier 1 Blankface practitioners were detained by Axiom security under a rarely-invoked 'identity obstruction' statute, which was subsequently challenged and overturned; the case is now standard curriculum in Meridian civil liberties education. The geneware relaxant component caused permanent facial muscle atrophy in an estimated 200 participants using unregulated formulations.
story_hooks: A character with permanent Blankface atrophy — someone who can no longer express emotion visibly — is being used as an unwilling icon by both activists and a fashion brand.
The Pale Grain collective's original manifesto contained technical specifications for a second-generation Blankface that defeats the new biometric systems; someone has found it.
A Tier 5 executive has quietly adopted Blankface for private meetings — the question is whether it's for privacy or because they're hiding something their natural expression would betray.
